title: A/R Detail lists the five buckets in fixed order and rows by name
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Make sure the report has open documents in all five aging buckets on today's date.
  • Make sure that in the "1-30 days past due" bucket, customer A has one open invoice, invoice A, and customer B has two, invoice B and invoice C. Customer B's name comes first alphabetically, and invoice B's number is smaller than invoice C's but has fewer digits.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
custom_steps:
1. Read the bucket rows from top to bottom without expanding anything.
  2. Look at the header of the "Customer Full Name" column.
  3. Click the chevron of the "1-30 days past due" bucket to expand it.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The buckets read, in this order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current".

Step 2:

  • "Customer Full Name" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 3:

  • The bucket opens and shows its rows: customer B's two invoices come first, invoice B above invoice C (smaller number first, counted as a number), then customer A's invoice A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
